findings.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss:291 — P2, confidence 100: `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%));` The reply-author link changes from the prior 30% primary shade to 70% in light themes and 30% secondary in dark themes, reversing the intended lightness mapping and rendering this semantic label at the wrong contrast in both theme branches.

app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/user.scss:522 — P2, confidence 100: `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%));` The group-member name loses its prior 30% primary/70% secondary mapping and becomes the 50% title shade, collapsing two distinct semantic text levels and regressing contrast in both themes.

app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss:102 — P2, confidence 100: `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%));` The mobile message-length hint reverses its prior 70% primary/30% secondary mapping, so it receives the opposite contrast role from the desktop modal and the dark-theme correction becomes a cross-platform visual regression.

app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss:182 — P2, confidence 100: `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%));` The mobile topic-card heading loses its prior 20% primary/80% secondary mapping and becomes the 50% subtitle shade, collapsing the card hierarchy and reducing heading contrast in both theme branches.
